sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 7:43

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 7:43:1
items.html: Hesed drew the five Hassadim to expand in the Guf of Aba, as is known, and when he died he descended to Beria, and the five lights descended into Gevura, into the third king, and then the backs of Aba fell: For in the breaking of the king of Hesed, phase three was refined to phase two, the level of Hochma vanished, and ten Sefirot came out at the level of Bina, as above. It is therefore regarded that Hochma turned its face into posterior, for the discernment of Bina is reckoned as the posterior of Hochma, even though it is the face of Bina herself. And this is what he says: “Aba turned his posterior to the face of Bina.”

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 7:43:2
items.html: Aba turned his backs to the face of Bina, and this discernment is called “back within face”, for the face of Bina stands opposite the backs of Hochma: For the face of Ima is the secret of the five Gevurot, as the ARI writes below, and they are sweetened by the light of Hassadim of Aba, as he wrote concerning the degree of back to face above (page 500, the passage beginning “Above,” study it there well). And one should not raise a difficulty from what the ARI says there (page 502, item 25), that the degree of back to face does not apply in AVI, for there the discussion is about the correction of AVI in the world of Atzilut, and then they have no need of it, as written in the Inner Light. Here, however, the discussion is about the diminution of the lights and their ascent to the Emanator according to the order of the degrees, and here it makes no difference at all whether they need it or not. And this is simple.
